terms.definitionEn: A file treated as an isolated scope because it uses import or export syntax.
terms.definitionAr: ملف بيتعامل معاه كنطاق مستقل لأنه بيستخدم صياغة import أو export.

terms.definitionEn: A declaration modifier that makes a value or type available to other modules.
terms.definitionAr: modifier بيخلي value أو type متاح لملفات modules تانية.
terms.example: export function add(a: number, b: number) { return a + b; }

terms.definitionEn: An exported member imported by its declared name, with optional renaming at the import site.
terms.definitionAr: عضو بيتصدر ويتستورد باسمه المعلن، وممكن يتغير اسمه وقت الاستيراد.

terms.definitionEn: The designated module value that an importer may bind to a chosen local name.
terms.definitionAr: القيمة المميزة في الـ module واللي المستورد يقدر يربطها باسم محلي يختاره.

terms.definitionEn: A declaration that brings exported values or types into the current module scope.
terms.definitionAr: تعريف بيدخل values أو types متصدرة لنطاق الـ module الحالي.

terms.definitionEn: An import form explicitly restricted to type use and erased from emitted JavaScript.
terms.definitionAr: صياغة import مخصصة لاستخدام النوع وبتتشال من JavaScript الناتج.

terms.definitionEn: A project configuration file where TypeScript compiler options and file inclusion can be specified.
terms.definitionAr: ملف إعدادات للمشروع ممكن تحدد فيه خيارات compiler والملفات الداخلة في البناء.

terms.definitionEn: A compiler option that enables a family of stronger type-checking options.
terms.definitionAr: خيار compiler بيفعل مجموعة من خيارات فحص الأنواع الأكثر صرامة.

terms.definitionEn: A compiler option selecting the JavaScript language feature level used for emitted output.
terms.definitionAr: خيار compiler بيحدد مستوى خصائص JavaScript في الكود الناتج.

terms.definitionEn: A compiler setting that controls the module-system form of generated JavaScript and related resolution behavior.
terms.definitionAr: إعداد compiler بيتحكم في صيغة نظام modules في JavaScript الناتج وسلوك resolution المرتبط.

terms.definitionEn: A compiler option that reports locations where an any type would otherwise be inferred implicitly.
terms.definitionAr: خيار compiler بيبلغ عن أماكن كان هيتم فيها استنتاج any من غير تصريح.

terms.definitionEn: The compiler process for locating files that correspond to module specifiers in imports.
terms.definitionAr: طريقة الـ compiler في تحديد الملفات الموافقة لمسارات modules في import.

questions.question: What does export make available?
options: The declared binding for importing modules
A new global variable in every source file
A runtime class generated from the constant
A default export that can be imported under any name
questions.explanation: export exposes the named binding to other modules.
questions.explanationAr: export بتخلي الـ binding المسمى متاح للـ modules التانية.

questions.question: Which export form does this syntax request?
options: The module's default export, renamed to add
The named export called add
Every export from the module under one namespace
A type-only member regardless of its declaration
questions.explanation: Braces request a named export with the matching exported name.
questions.explanationAr: الأقواس المعقوفة بتطلب named export بنفس الاسم.

questions.question: What kind of export is declared?
options: A named export that must be imported as create
A type-only export erased from all output
The module's default export
A namespace containing every module member
questions.explanation: The default keyword marks the module's default export.
questions.explanationAr: كلمة default بتحدد التصدير الافتراضي للـ module.

questions.question: What happens to this import in emitted JavaScript?
options: It loads the User class whenever the program starts
It becomes a runtime variable with an undefined value
It is converted into a default import automatically
It is erased because it is restricted to type use
questions.explanation: An import type is for type positions and is erased from JavaScript output.
questions.explanationAr: import type مخصص لمواضع الأنواع وبيتشال من JavaScript الناتج.

questions.question: What does this setting enable?
options: A family of stricter type-checking options
Automatic runtime validation for every object
Compilation of all JavaScript files without checks
A requirement that every import use a default export
questions.explanation: strict enables a suite of stronger checking options, including strict null checks.
questions.explanationAr: strict بيفعل مجموعة فحوصات أقوى، ومنها فحص null الصارم.

questions.question: What does target primarily affect?
options: The folder where source files are stored and where compiler output is written
The JavaScript feature level used for emitted code
The names that can be used in import declarations and their aliases
The runtime type of every exported function after the program starts
questions.explanation: target selects the JavaScript language level for output transformations.
questions.explanationAr: target بيحدد مستوى JavaScript للكود الناتج والتحويلات.

questions.question: What does this option report?
options: Every explicit annotation that uses any, even when deliberately written
Every value that might be null at runtime, regardless of its declared type
Locations where any would otherwise be inferred implicitly
All functions whose return type is omitted, even when safely inferred
questions.explanation: noImplicitAny reports places where an implicit any would be inferred.
questions.explanationAr: noImplicitAny بيبلغ عن الأماكن اللي كان هيتستنتج فيها any ضمنيًا.

questions.question: What does the module option configure?
options: Whether functions use strict parameter checking
The directory where declaration files are generated
The type of the default export in each source file
The module-system form of emitted JavaScript
questions.explanation: module controls the module format and interacts with module resolution settings.
questions.explanationAr: module بيتحكم في صيغة modules وبيتفاعل مع إعدادات resolution.

questions.code:
import type { Shape } from './shape.js';
let value: Shape;
questions.question: Why is Shape not a runtime value in this code?
options: The type-only import is erased from the emitted JavaScript
Every imported interface becomes a global variable instead
The module option removes all declarations from source files
A type alias is converted into a default export
questions.explanation: import type can only be used as a type and does not create a runtime binding.
questions.explanationAr: import type بيتستخدم كنوع بس ومش بيعمل binding وقت التشغيل.

questions.question: How many named values does this line export?
options: One
Zero because export is erased
Three
One default value
questions.explanation: The declaration exports one named binding, count.
questions.explanationAr: التعريف بيصدر binding واحد اسمه count.

questions.question: What runtime import remains for this type-only statement?
options: One default import
None
One named runtime binding
A namespace object
questions.explanation: Type-only imports are removed from emitted JavaScript.
questions.explanationAr: الـ imports الخاصة بالأنواع بس بتتشال من JavaScript الناتج.

questions.question: With noImplicitAny enabled and no parameter annotation, what is the type-check result?
questions.explanation: The unannotated parameter would otherwise receive an implicit any type.
questions.explanationAr: الـ parameter من غير annotation كان هياخد any ضمني.

questions.prompt: Expose this binding to other modules by name.
questions.explanation: export makes the binding available to importing modules.
questions.explanationAr: export بتخلي الـ binding متاح للـ modules المستوردة.

questions.prompt: Import the named function called add.
questions.explanation: The identifier inside braces names the requested export.
questions.explanationAr: الاسم جوه الأقواس بيحدد الـ export المطلوب.

questions.prompt: Import the declaration for use only as a type.
questions.explanation: The type modifier makes the import explicitly type-only.
questions.explanationAr: modifier type بيخلي الاستيراد مخصص للأنواع.

questions.prompt: Enable the strict option family in this project.
questions.explanation: strict enables the compiler's strict checking options.
questions.explanationAr: strict بيفعل خيارات الفحص الصارمة للـ compiler.

questions.prompt: Choose the ECMAScript level for emitted JavaScript.
questions.explanation: target accepts a JavaScript language level such as ES2022.
questions.explanationAr: target بيقبل مستوى لغة JavaScript زي ES2022.

questions.prompt: Report implicit any types during checking.
questions.explanation: noImplicitAny reports places where inference would produce any implicitly.
questions.explanationAr: noImplicitAny بيبلغ عن أماكن الاستنتاج الضمني لـ any.

questions.prompt: Set the emitted module format to ES modules.
questions.explanation: The module option selects the module-system output format.
questions.explanationAr: خيار module بيحدد صيغة نظام modules في الناتج.

questions.prompt: Mark the single exported function as the module default.
questions.explanation: export default declares a module's default export.
questions.explanationAr: export default بتعرف التصدير الافتراضي للـ module.

questions.question: How does an import or export affect whether a source file is treated as a module?
keyPoints: Top-level import or export syntax marks a module boundary
Module declarations are scoped to that module
Files without module syntax may be treated as scripts depending on configuration
questions.modelAnswer: A source file containing top-level import or export syntax is treated as a module, so its declarations are scoped to that module rather than shared as script globals. Files without such syntax may be treated as scripts, subject to project settings such as module detection. This distinction helps prevent accidental global name collisions.
questions.explanation: Module classification affects declaration scope and name sharing across files.
questions.explanationAr: تصنيف الملف كـ module بيأثر على نطاق التعريفات ومشاركة الأسماء بين الملفات.

questions.question: Why use import type when a dependency is needed only for annotations?
keyPoints: It is erased from emitted JavaScript
It can help control runtime module dependencies
questions.modelAnswer: import type makes it clear that the imported declaration is needed only for type checking. It is erased from emitted JavaScript, so it does not create a runtime import for that declaration. This can help keep runtime dependency graphs intentional.
questions.explanation: Explicit type-only syntax separates compile-time dependencies from runtime imports.
questions.explanationAr: الصياغة الصريحة بتفصل اعتماد الترجمة عن imports وقت التشغيل.

questions.question: What is the purpose of the strict compiler option?
keyPoints: It enables a suite of stricter checks
It includes options such as strictNullChecks and noImplicitAny
Individual strict options can also be configured
questions.modelAnswer: strict is a convenient umbrella that enables a family of stricter type-checking options. That family includes checks such as strictNullChecks and noImplicitAny. Projects can also configure individual strictness options when needed, but stricter settings often reveal issues that should be addressed.
questions.explanation: The option is an umbrella for several related checks rather than one single rule.
questions.explanationAr: الخيار ده بيجمع فحوصات مرتبطة، مش قاعدة واحدة بس.

questions.question: How should a project choose target and module settings?
keyPoints: target concerns JavaScript language output level
module concerns module-system output and resolution
Runtime and bundler support influence the choice
questions.modelAnswer: target selects the JavaScript language level TypeScript emits or preserves, while module controls module-system output and related resolution behavior. The right settings depend on the supported runtimes and whether a bundler or runtime resolves imports. They should match the project's deployment toolchain rather than be chosen independently of it.
questions.explanation: Both settings affect emitted code and should align with the host toolchain.
questions.explanationAr: الإعدادين بيأثروا على الكود الناتج ولازم يناسبوا أدوات التشغيل والبناء.
